clue.text: Plaything made nippers go without sleep

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
made in the sense of reworked, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: A toy that made small children go without their nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. Nippers is British slang for small children, and kip British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipping rope is a children's toy for jumping over as it swings.

clue.text: Substitute for blood vessel finished

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: Something stands in for a blood vessel that has run its course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato sauce is the classic fake gore of cheap stage and film productions.

clue.text: Those taking precedence abandoning it for religious domiciles

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the following word is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: priorities are the matters that come first

explanation.surface: People who come first give up their place in exchange for homes in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Priories are houses where monks or nuns live under a prior or prioress.

clue.text: One late detailed notion

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: de-tailed means its tail is cut off, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: the late are the dead

explanation.surface: A single belated thought, spelled out in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the last D from DEAD, leaving DEA; the surface reads it as elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or concept, a synonym of notion.

clue.text: Large masks produced for worker with bottle

indicators.note: produced in the sense of fashioned, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Big masks are made for a courageous labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges LARGE MASKS. Bottle is British slang for nerve, so 'worker with bottle' sounds like a brave one.
explanation.definitionFit: A glassmaker produces glass items such as bottles; the clue hides that under bottle meaning courage.

clue.text: Layer round the area

parts.note: O is round in shape
a zone is an area or region

explanation.surface: A coat applied around the region.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer is the band of the upper atmosphere that absorbs ultraviolet light.

clue.text: English language inspires love and joy

indicators.note: inspires means breathes in, so the language takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: Latin is a language
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: The English tongue breathes romance and happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness, near to joy.

clue.text: Bond girl could change to be ghastly

indicators.note: change tells us the letters before it are altered into another order

explanation.surface: A 007 heroine might transform into something hideous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bloodcurdling is horrifying enough to chill the blood, as ghastly things are.

clue.text: Idealistic situation interpreting ideals as proof

indicators.note: interpreting means reading in a new way, so the following letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone taking their ideals as evidence of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool's paradise is a state of happiness built on illusion, an unrealistic idyll.

clue.text: John finds Dicky reliant

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or weak, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A man called John learns that his weak heart depends on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' rearranges RELIANT; it is no name here. John is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, which slang calls a john.

clue.text: Fruit and eggs sent back for rat and duck

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the word before it is read the other way

parts.note: ova are eggs
a rat and a cad are both treacherous men
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, written O

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a meal of eggs on finding it was rat and duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped fruit with buttery green flesh.

clue.text: Alternative retains the alternative

indicators.note: retains means holds onto, so the conjunction keeps the following word inside

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: One choice keeps the other in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Other as an adjective means different or remaining, a second choice.

clue.text: Notable mixture of ale and spice

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A remarkable blend of beer and spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is an old word for special, outstanding.

clue.text: Sheep with single rash needing treatment

indicators.note: needing treatment suggests something to be worked on, so the letters are processed into another order

explanation.surface: A sheep with one skin outbreak calls for the vet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearlings are young sheep that have been shorn once.

clue.text: Detective Chief Inspector is a snake

parts.note: a copper is a police officer, here a detective
a chief, the head, of the inspectors

explanation.surface: A senior police officer turns out to be a treacherous person.
explanation.definitionFit: The copperhead is a venomous North American viper with a coppery head.

clue.text: Break in game

definitions.meaning: to break suddenly with a crack
a card game where players shout on matching cards

explanation.surface: A pause during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap means to break cleanly, and it is also a children's card game.

clue.text: Document to expire on opening

parts.note: to pass away is to die, so pass means expire
a port is an opening, as in a porthole

explanation.surface: Paperwork that runs out on the day it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official travel document proving identity and nationality.

clue.text: Bird to complain at bar

explanation.surface: A bird objects in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a marsh bird, to rail at is to rant, and a rail is a rod.

clue.text: Life is lapsing, heading to the bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the head letter moves to the foot, going to the bottom

parts.note: lapsing morally is sinning

explanation.surface: Existence is declining as it sinks to its lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading to the bottom' moves the first S of SINNING to the end. An innings is a cricket batter's turn, used for a lifetime ('a good innings').
explanation.definitionFit: A good innings is British idiom for a long life, so innings stands for a lifespan.

clue.text: Flame thrown by player, criminal

indicators.note: thrown as in thrown into disorder, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: An actor's fire-throwing turns out to be a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits crimes.

clue.text: Wedding speaker and his unimaginative present

definitions.meaning: someone who proposes a toast at a reception
a bread-browning gadget, the stock dull wedding gift

explanation.surface: The best man and his dull wedding gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster proposes toasts, and a bread toaster is the cliché wedding present.

clue.text: He is no fellow for circulating

definitions.text: He is no fellow for circulating

indicators.note: circulating means moving round, so the letters are spun into a different order

explanation.surface: A man who is not one to mingle with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' rearranges NO FELLOW; the whole clue also describes the answer, a loner who doesn't mingle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lone wolf keeps to himself, with no companions, and does not work a room.

clue.text: Drag forcibly from sleep, we hear

indicators.note: we hear points to a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: rest is sleep or repose

explanation.surface: Someone is dragged out of slumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals a homophone: REST and WREST sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to pull something away with a violent twist.

clue.text: Cope with position

definitions.meaning: a stance or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: Handling one's post.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to bear it, and a stand is a stated view.

clue.text: City-centre of anagrams

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, which are taken here

explanation.surface: The heart of a puzzle full of jumbled words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle four letters of ANAGRAMS. The surface hyphen joins City-centre, but City is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Granny cutting fabric

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
a cutting or keen edge is sharp

explanation.surface: Grandma snipping cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: Vocal equipment starts to go, leaving our tonsils to inflame, sadly

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the opening letter of each following word is used

explanation.surface: A singer's voice is failing as inflamed tonsils take hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the initials of GO LEAVING OUR TONSILS TO INFLAME SADLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The glottis is the opening between the vocal cords in the larynx.

clue.text: During school tests, one works OK

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the next piece is set inside the tests

parts.note: SATs are standardised school tests
I is the Roman numeral for one
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: In exams, a student's efforts are just about acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory means adequate or acceptable, as OK does.
